g.text: Read the diagram and study where each part sits.

Use Check Answer to grade your placement.

svg.text: Tip: petals & sepals are the outer whorls; stamens (male) and the pistil (female) sit inside.

g.text: Petal — colourful part that attracts pollinators.
Sepal — green leaf-like part protecting the bud.
Filament — stalk that holds the anther.
Pistil — female organ: stigma, style, ovary.
Stigma — sticky top that catches pollen.
Style — tube guiding pollen to the ovary.
Ovary — swollen base holding the ovules.
Receptacle — base that supports all parts.

svg.text: Mnemonic: “Pistil has a sticky Stigma, a long Style, and an Ovary below.”
Click a tile to place it on the diagram · click a placed label to return it

g.text: Pollen travels from the anther to the stigma, then travels down the style to the ovary.
After fertilisation, the ovary matures into a fruit and the ovules become seeds.
• Petals (pink) and sepals (green) form the outer whorls.
• The stamen is the male part: anther on top of a filament.
• The pistil is the female part: stigma → style → ovary.
• The ovary is the swollen base of the pistil.
• The receptacle is the little shelf the flower sits on.
Compare your placed labels with the key below.
A placement is correct when the arrow points to the exact structure.
Common mix-ups: anther vs. stigma (both at the tips), and
ovary vs. receptacle (both at the base).
